clue.text: With game almost finished, sign on for county

indicators.note: almost finished says the game's name stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: chess is a board game
to sign on a worker is to hire them

explanation.surface: Late in a match, someone is recruited to play for a county side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost finished' cuts the last letter from the game. Cheshire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheshire is one of the shires of England, an administrative region of the kind called a county.

clue.text: War film about doctor

indicators.note: about says the film wraps round the doctor

parts.note: a film is a thin coat or layer
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A war movie about a medic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is a thin layer, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting between armed forces, as in war.

clue.text: Gipsy girl dares male to misbehave

indicators.note: to misbehave says the letters of the next words behave badly and rearrange

explanation.surface: A Romany girl provokes a man into bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: DARESMALE rearranged gives ESMERALDA, the gipsy heroine of Victor Hugo's The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.
explanation.definitionFit: Esmeralda is the Romani dancer in Victor Hugo's novel about the bell-ringer of Notre-Dame.

clue.text: Worker on strike gets basic provision

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in a farmhand
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: A striking employee receives minimal support.
explanation.definitionFit: A dole of food, money or goods given free to those in need.

clue.text: Way rook circles over perch

indicators.note: in a down clue, over says the rook and circles sit above the way

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
O is a circle, so two circles are OO
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A rook flies round above the road looking for a perch.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where birds settle to rest.

clue.text: Object to work attitude

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work of music
a pose is an attitude struck

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the posture they must hold at work.
explanation.definitionFit: To object to something is to resist or argue against it.

clue.text: At foot of page there's careless assumption

indicators.note: in a down clue, at foot of says the careless word sits below the page

parts.note: remiss means careless or negligent

explanation.surface: A footnote shows a careless assumption by the author.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiss is a proposition taken as given in an argument, an assumption.

clue.text: Eccentric and, to some extent, without reason

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone acting oddly, and partly without reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional or bizarre, beyond the usual bounds.

clue.text: 'Those no longer performing may be demanding types'

definitions.meaning: ... are former actors who no longer perform
people who demand payment or obedience

explanation.surface: Retired performers can be rather demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it is former actors; whole, it means those who demand what is owed.

clue.text: Letter combinations author initially placed in special grids

annotationWithheld.why: Letter combinations author initially placed in special grids (8): A (author initially) in an anagram of GRIDS gives only six letters; nothing in the clue as printed supplies the P and H of DIGRAPHS
annotationWithheld.clue: Letter combinations author initially placed in special grids

clue.text: Something physics teacher talks about when one nods off?

definitions.text: Something physics teacher talks about when one nods off?

parts.words: Something physics teacher talks about when one nods off?
parts.note: a term from mechanics for a body's resistance to turning, reread as the instant a dozing pupil goes still

explanation.surface: A science lesson so dull that a pupil falls asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The physics term, read literally, is an instant of sluggish stillness, which is what dozing off is.

clue.text: Two bearings needed to get to endpoint of journey?

parts.note: air means a person's manner or bearing
port also means bearing, the way one carries oneself, as in deportment

explanation.surface: A navigator needs two compass readings to reach the end of a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearings' suggests compass directions, but here it means demeanour: AIR and PORT are two words for how one carries oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight ends at a terminal for aircraft, so it is where an air journey finishes.

clue.text: Fit chaps into right clothes

indicators.note: into says the next pieces go inside the word for right

parts.note: A1, written AI, means in top condition, fit
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A tailor makes sure the men's outfits fit properly.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning top-class or fit, is written with the letter I standing for the figure 1, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: Working-class clergy excel

parts.note: the cloth is a collective term for the clergy
to cap something is to outdo or excel it

explanation.surface: A claim that ordinary working clerics outshine their grander colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: A CLOTH CAP is the flat cap that is a British emblem of the working man.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat cap is a symbol of the labouring man, so the phrase is used as an adjective meaning proletarian.

clue.text: Movie presentation that's peculiarly American

indicators.note: peculiarly says the letters of the next word are arranged in a strange way

explanation.surface: A film format that is very much a US thing.
explanation.walkthrough: AMERICAN rearranged gives CINERAMA, a widescreen film format from the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinerama was a widescreen process for projecting films on a curved screen.

clue.text: Lofted shot more dangerous? Right, one can get out

indicators.note: get out tells the solver that the letters for the next words leave the longer word

parts.note: riskier means more dangerous
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A batsman's high hit is risky, since a fielder may catch him out.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface leads to the cricket answer: a SKIER is a ball hit high in the air, easily caught. R and I leave RISKIER.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a ball skied high into the air is called by this name.

clue.text: Provoke in the street one football crowd

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
I is the Roman numeral one
the gate is the attendance at a football match

explanation.surface: A football supporter stirs up trouble on the road outside the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to bring about or incite, as one provokes a reaction.

clue.text: Sitting tenant? Not legally so

parts.note: someone who occupies a property, crouching or otherwise, with no lease or right to be there

explanation.surface: A question about the legal status of a sitting tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who occupies empty property without the right to do so; one squatting also sits.

clue.text: Measure five twenty-eighths?

parts.note: seven twenty-eighths is a fourth part; the unit wanted is that word with only five of its seven letters, a liquid measure

explanation.surface: An odd fraction to measure out.
explanation.walkthrough: Seven twenty-eighths is a quarter; QUARTER has seven letters, and five of them give QUART, a quarter of a gallon.
explanation.definitionFit: This liquid unit is two pints, a fourth of a gallon.

clue.text: From end of giant insect, strange wax appears

indicators.note: end of says only the last letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: an ant is an insect
rum is British slang for strange

explanation.surface: Some odd wax oozes out of the back of a huge bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wax' is not the substance but the old sense of a fit of anger, as in 'get in a wax'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax is dated British slang for a fit of temper.

clue.text: Most unpleasant wine kept in the home

indicators.note: kept in says the wine is stored inside the word for home

parts.note: a nest is a home, as in leaving the nest
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: The worst wine of all is the one stored in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of nasty, meaning the most disagreeable.

clue.text: One may have secret knowledge making home brew, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the letters are what the words sound like, not how they are spelt

parts.note: in means home, and cider is a brew, together sounding like the answer

explanation.surface: A home brewer may know some secrets of the trade.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is a person within an organisation who has private information.

clue.text: Dealer putting up, for example, Titian paintings

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up says the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Titian is a reddish-gold colour, named after the Venetian painter
paintings are art

explanation.surface: An art dealer hangs some works by Titian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titian' looks like the painter but is a hair colour, RED; 'putting up' turns RED + ART to give TRADER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader buys and sells goods, as a dealer does.

clue.text: A recluse gets hold of married social-worker

indicators.note: gets hold of says the recluse's word grips the next letter inside it

parts.note: a loner is a recluse

explanation.surface: A hermit finds himself a wife who works for the welfare services.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was a hospital official in Britain who looked after patients' welfare, an early medical social worker.

clue.text: Proper society events in the ' countryside

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or proper

explanation.surface: Respectable society gatherings take place in rural areas.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunts gather at MEETS, assemblies of riders and hounds before a hunt in the British countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting gatherings in rural Britain are called meets.

clue.text: Money needed by the Queen to cover one fire

parts.note: cash is money
I is the Roman numeral one
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Royal funds are needed to insure against a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like a blaze but is the verb, to sack.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss him from service, to sack him.

clue.text: Rank team-leader assumed in action

indicators.note: assumed in says the leading letter is taken inside the word for action

parts.note: a case is a legal action or lawsuit

indicators.note: leader says only the first letter of the word it is attached to is wanted

explanation.surface: A captain is given a rank once he joins the fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, a rank in society.

clue.text: Grounds for an optimistic outlook

parts.note: grounds read as territory: the land pledged to the Israelites in the Bible, a phrase for any hoped-for paradise

explanation.surface: Reasons to be cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaan, the territory pledged by God, is a byword for a hoped-for happy future.

clue.text: English thinker reflected, becoming abstract

indicators.note: reflected says the letters are read as in a mirror, from the end back

parts.note: a muser is someone who thinks or ponders

explanation.surface: An English philosopher meditates and drifts off into abstraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns E + MUSER round to give RESUME; 'abstract' is the noun, a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: A résumé is a summary of a text, which is what an abstract is.

clue.text: Repeatedly try to show agreement

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word is given more than once

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: Keep trying to demonstrate that you agree.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled cry is how MPs voice assent in Parliament.
